### SetMaxResponseBodySize

Sets the largest response body the client buffers, in bytes. A response that declares or sends more fails with `fasthttp.ErrBodyTooLarge`. A client from `New`, the default client behind the package-level helpers included, starts at 100 MiB; a client built around a `fasthttp.Client`, `HostClient` or `LBClient` keeps that client's `MaxResponseBodySize`, which `fasthttp` leaves unlimited. Zero or less removes the limit. Call it before the first request: a `fasthttp.Client` gives each host the limit it has when it first serves that host. A body read through [response streaming](#response-streaming) is not buffered and not limited, which makes streaming the way to receive a larger one.

```go title="Signature"
func (c *Client) SetMaxResponseBodySize(size int) *Client
```

:::caution
`fasthttp` allocates a buffered body from the `Content-Length` or chunk size the server declares, before the body arrives. Without a limit, a server can end the process with a response of a few bytes that declares a body too large to allocate: the Go runtime reports that as a fatal error, which `recover` cannot catch. Keep a limit for servers you do not control.
:::

The runtime helpers (`Do`, `DoRedirects`, `Forward`, `DomainForward` and `BalancerForward`) dispatch through a client that bounds every request: each request, and each hop `DoRedirects` follows, has 30 seconds for the whole exchange, the connect, the write and the read of the response included, in one attempt, and a response body of at most 100 MiB, which the proxy buffers whole or, for a response set to stream, relays up to that size, so an upstream that stalls or streams without end holds neither the handler nor the memory; a transfer that takes longer than the bound fails with it too. `DoTimeout` and `DoDeadline` set the bound of their own request, longer or shorter, and the time they allow, like `Config.Timeout`, covers the connect as well. For other bounds, hand the proxy a client with `ReadTimeout`, `WriteTimeout` and `MaxResponseBodySize` set, registered with `proxy.WithClient` or passed per call; it replaces the default client with its bounds, and fasthttp applies a client's read and write timeouts to each attempt it makes. A client that streams response bodies is held to its `MaxResponseBodySize` as well, which fasthttp ignores for a stream:

```go
proxy.WithClient(&fasthttp.Client{
    NoDefaultUserAgentHeader: true,
    DisablePathNormalizing:   true,
    ReadTimeout:              30 * time.Second,
    WriteTimeout:             10 * time.Second,
    MaxResponseBodySize:      10 << 20, // 10 MiB
})
```
